newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude flat, Brent players eye U.S. optio.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude flat, Brent players eye U.S. optio.

text.p: North Sea crude was becalmed on Monday with paper markets steady and spot traders waiting to see whether an arbitrage to the U.S. would open up, relieving some of the prompt pressure on prices.
July Brent fetched $19.41 a barrel, just a cent up on Friday's London close but about 10 cents weaker than a handful of trades in late U.S. dealing.

Intermonth paper spreads widened slightly, July/Aug easing to -14/-11 from trade at -12 cents late Friday, but dealers said the move had more to do with the general lack of interest than any real pressure on the front end of the Brent forward market.
Benchmark Dated Brent was steady as details emerged of a second trade on Friday at July Brent -30 cents. Two Brents were due to turn wet on Monday including a deferred June 14-16 cargo.
Traders said more players would be exploring arbitrage options later on Monday after a Brent fetched WTI -65 cents for early July delivery into the U.S. Gulf on Friday.
Shipping brokers said Shell fixed the VLCC Berge Nisa for a trans-Atlantic trip loading mid-June.
"Brent is pretty cheap at current levels which could make the arbitrage work but it is also starting to affect the other (North Sea) grades," said a trader.
Ekofisk traded Friday at Dated +17 cents, a cent cheaper than the previous reported deal.

In the Mediterranean, traders were waiting for the first June sales of Russian Urals to get underway as operations at the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk returned to normal after an oil spill last week.
Two large and four small first-decade Urals cargoes were on offer at around Dated Brent minus $1.35, traders said. But buying interest for that period looked slack, traders said.
"It seems that everyone has managed to postpone their requirements until the second half of June," said one.
Good supplies of other sours were seen for the second and third decade, while traders were still waiting to hear whether the U.N. would renew the Iraqi oil-for-food deal.
If the U.N. does agree to a rollover of the first six-month agreement which expires on June 7, fresh Iraqi exports flows are expected to resume in late June.
West African markets were fairly quiet, with just a handful of June cargoes still unsold, and July loading programmes yet to be released.
A third decade June Bonny Light was on offer at around Dated Brent plus 55 cents, a Brass River at Dated plus 58 cents, as well as Forcados in the low 20s and a Qua Iboe in the high 40s.
The Nigerian July crude loading programme was expected by mid-week.
Traders said that despite a widening Brent/Dubai spread and a well-supplied Far East market there was still some interest in early July barrels from Asian refiners.
"We should see some buying if it stays below a dollar," a trader said.
The August Brent/Dubai spread was talked at +80/+95 on Monday.
--Mark Thompson, Rosalind Russell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
